summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether total hip arthroplasty without subtrochanteric osteotomy is feasible in patients with Crowe III/IV developmental dysplasia.
summary_en.method: A retrospective analysis of clinical data from DDH patients undergoing THA was performed to assess surgical feasibility and complications.
summary_en.result: THA without subtrochanteric osteotomy is feasible in Crowe III/IV DDH patients with satisfactory clinical outcomes.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up data validated the surgical outcomes.

papers.title: Toward the digital twin of additive manufacturing: Integrating thermal simulations, sensing, and analytics to detect process faults
papers.abstract: The goal of this work is to achieve the defect-free production of parts made using Additive Manufacturing (AM) processes. As a step towards this goal, the objective is to detect flaws in AM parts during the process by combining predictions from a physical model (simulation) with in-situ sensor signatures in a machine learning framework. We hypothesize that flaws in AM parts are detected with significantly higher statistical fidelity (F-score) when both in-situ sensor data and theoretical predictions are pooled together in a machine learning model, compared to an approach that is based exclusively on machine learning of sensor data (black-box model) or physics-based predictions (white-box model). We test the hypothesized efficacy of such a gray-box model or digital twin approach in the context of the laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and directed energy deposition (DED) AM processes. For example, in the DED process, we first predicted the instantaneous spatiotemporal distribution of temperature in a thin-wall titanium alloy part using a computational heat transfer model based on graph theory. Subsequently, we combined the preceding physics-derived thermal trends with in-situ temperature measurements obtained from a pyrometer in a readily implemented supervised machine learning framework (support vector machine). We demonstrate that the integration of temperature predictions from an ab initio heat transfer model and in-situ sensor data is capable of detecting flaws in the DED-produced thin-wall part with F-score approaching 90%. By contrast, the F-score decreases to nearly 80% when either temperature measurements from the in-situ sensor or temperature distribution predictions from the theoretical model are used alone by themselves. This work thus demonstrates an early foray into the digital twin paradigm for real-time process monitoring in AM via seamless integration of physics-based modeling (simulation), in-situ sensing, and data analytics (machine learning).

summary_en.motivation: To achieve defect-free production in additive manufacturing by detecting flaws during the process.
summary_en.method: A gray-box model integrating physics-based thermal simulations with in-situ pyrometer measurements using a support vector machine.
summary_en.result: The integrated approach achieved an F-score of approximately 90%, outperforming both pure physics-based and pure data-driven models.
summary_en.validation: Validated on a DED titanium alloy thin-wall part, comparing against black-box and white-box models.

summary_en.motivation: To quantify the impact of correlated random parameters on the performance of MEMS devices.
summary_en.method: Polynomial chaos expansion is employed to handle correlated random parameters in uncertainty quantification.
summary_en.result: The method effectively captures the effect of parameter correlations on output uncertainty.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through simulation case studies of MEMS devices.

papers.title: Online Medical Data Stream Mining Based on Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Approaches
papers.abstract: Introduction. Data mining approaches in medical diagnostics tasks have a number of special properties that do not allow the use of such approaches in a classical form. That's why adaptive neuro-fuzzy systems for online medical data stream processing tasks and its learning algorithms have been developed. Proposed systems can process medical data streams in three modes: supervised learning, unsupervised learning and active learning.

summary_en.motivation: Medical data stream mining requires adaptive approaches due to special properties of diagnostic tasks.
summary_en.method: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy systems are developed for online medical data stream processing with three learning modes.
summary_en.result: The proposed systems can handle supervised, unsupervised, and active learning for medical data streams.

papers.title: The effects of hand soap making practice with addition of pineapple skin extract (Ananas comosus L. Merr) on learning interests in colloidal materials in senior high school
papers.abstract: Learning by practicum method is a way of delivering learning material by providing opportunities to the students to practicein order to make the students engage in planned and active learning experiences so that students' interest grows on chemistry subject. The population in this study were the students of XI class at YAPSI Senior High School in Medan. The sampling technique is done by using the Quota sampling technique. The instruments were the student’s interests in questionnaire and student activeness observation sheet. The requirements test is in the form of normality test and homogeneity test with the value of L count = 0.663 initial interests data and L count = 0.172 final interests data which means the data is normally distributed. In the homogeneity test F count = 0.233 initial interests data and F count = 0.449 final interests data with homogeneous results. The data analysis technique was done by using the hypothesis t test and N-gain test. The results showed that the hand soap making practice with the addition of pineapple extract ( Ananas comosus L .. Merr) had an influence on students’ learning interest with N-gain of 7.6 in experimental class data and N-gain of 5.4 in control class data and from the t hypothesis test obtained T count > T table which T count = 6.90 and T table at level 0.05 is 2.01 so H o is accepted, which means that there was an influence of the handsoap making practice with the addition of pineapple skin extract ( Ananas comosus L. Merr) on student interests in learning. Keywords: Colloid; hand soap making practice; interests

summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether a hands-on practice of making hand soap with pineapple skin extract can increase high school students' interest in learning colloidal materials.
summary_en.method: A quasi-experimental design was used with questionnaire and observation data, analyzed by t-test and N-gain score.
summary_en.result: The experimental group showed a higher increase in learning interest (N-gain 7.6) than the control group (N-gain 5.4), with a significant t-test result.
summary_en.validation: Normality and homogeneity tests were conducted, and hypothesis testing confirmed the effect.
